question: The force of attraction applied between molecules of the same substance is called:
solution:
The correct answer is __**cohesive force**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cohesive Forces:**

 
 
• These are the attractive forces between molecules of the same substance.
 
• In liquids, cohesive forces pull molecules together, keeping them in a relatively compact state.
 
• Stronger cohesive forces lead to higher surface tension.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adhesive Forces**:

 
 
• These are the attractive forces between molecules of different substances.
 
• For example, the adhesive forces between water molecules and the glass walls of a container allow water to wet the glass.
 
 
 
• **Capillarity:**
 
 
• **​** This phenomenon arises from the interplay of cohesive and adhesive forces.
 
• It refers to the ability of a liquid to flow in narrow spaces against the force of gravity. When adhesive forces are stronger than cohesive forces, the liquid tends to rise in a narrow tube (like a capillary).
 
 
 
• **Surface Tension:**
 
 
• This is the tendency of the surface of a liquid to contract to the smallest possible area.
 
• It's caused by the imbalance of forces acting on the surface molecules.
 
• Molecules at the surface experience a net inward force, pulling them together and creating a "skin" on the liquid's surface.
